findings.summary: A promotion can demote a person's urgent request that has no priority record
findings.evidence: `build_capped` fills urgent slots in uncapped order (rung, then age), and the only exempt items are those in `person_set`, meaning jobs with an `athena priority` record (drain.rs:4183-4193). A request a person filed with a `Priority: urgent` line has no priority record, so it is not in `person_set`. A promoted improvement item that ranks ahead of it can take its urgent slot, and the person's request is then demoted to high. The plan covers only the other direction (the promoted item being demoted), and its dependents entry says a person's priority is never lowered. Fix: Say in the Risks section and the CHANGELOG that a promotion can push a text-marked urgent request over the cap. Better: have `build_improving` count promoted items after the tier's original members when it applies the urgent cap, so a promotion never displaces an item that was urgent on its own. Add a plan.rs case that shows the chosen behavior.

findings.summary: Only one open request per repeated cause is found
findings.evidence: `addressing_request` returns one request per cause: the first open one, or else a landed or turned-down one. If a second open request cites the same cause's introspections, `improvement_of` does not list it. That request gets no improvement turn and no promotion, though it is linked the same way. Fix: In `improvement_of`, list every open request whose text cites one of the cause's introspection ids, using the same citation test as `addressing_request`, rather than only `RepeatedCause.request`. Or state the one-request-per-cause limit in the doc comment.

findings.summary: A hand-built `Report` in display.rs tests needs every field
findings.evidence: `drain::Report` derives only Debug, Clone, PartialEq and Serialize, not Default. Its only literal is at drain.rs:3057, so a hand-built `Report` in display.rs tests has to spell out every field. Fix: Build the report through a small test helper, or get it from the Stub drain run in tests/drain.rs, rather than writing a full literal in display.rs.
findings.location: Step 7 / Criterion 4: display.rs unit test that builds a `Report` by hand; crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:1100-1101

findings.summary: The main.rs help tests are missing from the dependents list
findings.evidence: `drain_help_follows_the_ceiling_it_is_built_from` checks that the drain after_help template keeps the `at most {ceiling})` placeholder. The edit to the Order paragraph must not touch that phrase. Fix: List the main.rs help tests as a dependent, and add a needle test for the new Order-paragraph sentence.

summary: Round 3 of the plan matches the request and the accepted reading. I read the code it names, and it exists as described: `Plan::build_capped` and `priority_violations` (plan.rs:518, 680), `Drain::prepare` as the single plan build that `drain_with` calls before each wave (drain.rs:2196, 2924, 2990), `batches_for` (2837), `tried.extend` (2981), the one `Report` literal (3057), `Shared` and `Rebasing` in tests/drain.rs (7183, 7228, 8083), `spec_request_is_open` (hestia.rs:677), `ThroughputProposal.request_job` (records.rs:2160), and the steward channel set only by `RequestQueue::apply` (steward.rs:654). The approach is sound. It fixes the ordering at the plan build. It finds improvement requests through recorded links, not title text, and says plainly that the slowdown request is not covered. The gap rule, together with `since_turn` and `tried`, gives the same remaining order on every replan, which answers the starvation risk from rebuilding before each wave. Splitting groups around a moved item keeps the one-in-three share under `drain_concurrent`. The demonstrations call production entry points: `build_improving`, `improvement_of`, `drain::plan`, `drain::drain` and `drain_concurrent`. They would fail without the behavior: they compare against `build_capped`, and the `Shared` companion run has no improvement items. The doubles only supply which ids are improvement requests. No athena.toml field is added, and the work fits one producer run. I found four minor or nit issues, none blocking. A promotion counted before the caps can push a person's text-marked urgent request (not in `person_set`) over the urgent cap. Only one open request per repeated cause is listed. A hand-built `Report` in display.rs tests needs every field. The main.rs help tests are missing from the dependents list.
